q: A kingdom is a subdivision of a domain.
e: True. A kingdom is a subdivision of a domain. Domains sit above kingdoms: Bacteria, Archaea, and Eukarya.

q: There are five kingdoms of living things.
e: False. It is not true that there are five kingdoms of living things. Many courses now use six kingdoms by splitting the bacteria.

q: Archaebacteria and Eubacteria are both prokaryotic kingdoms.
e: True. Archaebacteria and Eubacteria are both prokaryotic kingdoms. Prokaryotic cells have no nucleus; their DNA sits in the cytoplasm.

q: Eukarya includes only unicellular organisms.
e: False. It is not true that eukarya includes only unicellular organisms. Eukarya includes large multicellular plants and animals as well.

q: Viruses are included in the six kingdoms of living organisms.
e: False. It is not true that viruses are included in the six kingdoms of living organisms. Viruses are not members of the living kingdoms.

q: Fungi can be unicellular or multicellular.
e: True. Fungi can be unicellular or multicellular. A multicellular organism is made of many cells that share the work of life.

q: Plants are classified under the kingdom Animalia.
e: False. It is not true that plants are classified under the kingdom Animalia. Plants belong to Plantae, not Animalia.

q: Animalia includes multicellular organisms that are heterotrophic.
e: True. Animalia includes multicellular organisms that are heterotrophic. Heterotrophs must take in food made by other organisms.

q: Eubacteria are known for their complex cellular structure.
e: False. It is not true that eubacteria are known for their complex cellular structure. Eubacteria are prokaryotes with a simple cell plan and no nucleus.

q: The kingdom Protista contains unicellular and colonial groups.
e: True. The kingdom Protista contains unicellular and colonial groups. A unicellular organism is a whole living thing made of one cell.

q: All organisms in the kingdom Fungi can photosynthesize.
e: False. It is not true that all organisms in the kingdom Fungi can photosynthesize. Not all organisms in the kingdom Fungi can photosynthesize.

q: The kingdom Plantae consists of eukaryotic organisms.
e: True. The kingdom Plantae consists of eukaryotic organisms. Plantae contains photosynthetic organisms with cellulose walls and chlorophyll.

q: The characteristics of the kingdoms are the same for all.
e: False. It is not true that the characteristics of the kingdoms are the same for all. Each kingdom is defined by its own set of traits.

q: Viruses can reproduce independently outside of host cells.
e: False. It is not true that viruses can reproduce independently outside of host cells. Viruses reproduce only inside a host cell.

q: The kingdom Animalia includes organisms that are autotrophic.
e: False. It is not true that the kingdom Animalia includes organisms that are autotrophic. The kingdom Animalia includes organisms that are not autotrophic.

q: The kingdom Protista includes both autotrophs and heterotrophs.
e: True. The kingdom Protista includes both autotrophs and heterotrophs. That is how this part of the lesson is stated.

q: All organisms in the kingdom Plantae are multicellular.
e: False. It is not true that all organisms in the kingdom Plantae are multicellular. Not all organisms in the kingdom Plantae are multicellular.

q: The kingdom Fungi is characterized by the presence of chlorophyll.
e: False. It is not true that the kingdom Fungi is characterized by the presence of chlorophyll. The kingdom Fungi is not characterized by the presence of chlorophyll.

q: Eubacteria can reproduce asexually by fission.
e: True. Eubacteria can reproduce asexually by fission. Eubacteria are prokaryotes with a relatively simple cell structure.

q: The classification of organisms is fixed and does not change over time.
e: False. It is not true that the classification of organisms is fixed and does not change over time. The classification of organisms is revised when new evidence appears over time.

q: Viruses are classified within the kingdoms of living organisms.
e: False. It is not true that viruses are classified within the kingdoms of living organisms. Viruses are not classified within the kingdoms of living organisms.
